mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The potential for severe storms capable of large hail and severe wind gusts is expected to increase this afternoon into evening. A severe thunderstorm watch is possible

details.label: Summary
details.text: The potential for severe storms capable of large hail and severe wind gusts is expected to increase this afternoon into evening. A severe thunderstorm watch is possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Visible satellite imagery and lightning data indicate thunderstorms developing over the central Rockies, including the CO Front Range, with additional storms noted over central into northeast WY, and the far northwest NE Panhandle. More widespread cloud cover has slowed daytime heating across portions of the adjacent High Plains, where latest objective analysis indicates lingering convective inhibition. However, continued daytime heating should allow the cap to weaken, thereby allowing storms to advance into the High Plains, amidst a steep lapse rate environment featuring MLCAPE of 1000-1500 J/kg. When coupled with 30-40 kt of deep-layer shear, the setup will support multicell and some supercell storm modes capable of mainly large hail initially. Latest CAM guidance continues to suggest that storms will grow upscale into clusters this evening with an associated increase in severe wind gust potential

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.00-1.75 IN

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Isolated severe storm potential appears to be increasing across the area. Convective trends are being monitored for a possible watch

details.label: Summary
details.text: Isolated severe storm potential appears to be increasing across the area. Convective trends are being monitored for a possible watch

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Renewed thunderstorm development is underway along the southern flank of a recently decayed nocturnal MCS from south of Wilmington to the Cincinnati vicinity. Stronger heating along the southern periphery of the residual cloud canopy has allowed temperatures to warm into the mid 80s to lower 90s, which, coupled with dewpoints in the mid 70s, is yielding MLCAPE of 2000-2500 J/kg. Stronger forcing for ascent and vertical shear remain displaced to the northwest of the area, in closer proximity to an MCV over northwest IN, leading to uncertainty in the extent of the severe storm threat in the near term. However, the character of the thermodynamic environment suggests some potential for locally damaging wind gusts with the current storms this afternoon over the next 1-2 hours. A comparatively greater severe storm risk may materialize later this afternoon into evening with the arrival of the stronger forcing for ascent and vertical shear. Between now and then, convective trends are being monitored for signs of storm organization, which would warrant consideration of a watch issuance

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...UP TO 60 MPH
